Hi all  quick summary / answers to the questionnaire items Marissa flagged. I'll populate the Excel sheet and attach a short README for exports. Attaching draft answers + export instructions.

Summary (high-level):
- Admin activity logs: we capture actor identity (user id & role), action type (create/update/delete/config), resource id, timestamp (ISO8601 UTC), source IP, region, and request id. Logs are retained per-customer policy; default retention 90 days, configurable to 7/30/90/365.
- API logs: request metadata (method, endpoint, model id, token usage, latency, request id). We do not persist full user request payloads by default unless enabled via enterprise audit mode (explicit opt-in). Responses are treated similarly  metadata stored; full output can be retained if customer opts in with appropriate contractual terms.
- Exportability: we support scheduled exports to customer S3 buckets (AES-256 encrypted), ad-hoc CSV/JSON dumps via Console, and streaming to customer endpoints (webhook). We can provide a pre-signed S3 transfer and automated exports on a daily/hourly cadence.
- Immutability: standard logs are append-only within our logging system. For audit-grade immutability (WORM), we offer an option to push archival copies to a write-once S3 bucket or an external WORM provider; we can also notarize checksums on an external timeline for stronger guarantees.
- SOC 2: Redwood is currently undergoing SOC 2 Type II audit; controls are implemented and Type II is on track for completion in Q4 2027. We can provide the SOC 2 interim bridge letter and the Type I report on request.

Attachments: acme_vendor_questionnaire.xlsx (completed draft), audit_logging_export_instructions.md

I'll attach the completed questionnaire to this thread and Marissa can send to Alex. Happy to hop on a quick call with Acme's security team if they want a walkthrough.
